simple.meaning: אָנַק (ʼânaq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to shriek.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Jeremiah, Ezekiel, beginning at Jeremiah 51:52. The surrounding contexts include city, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָנַק (H602) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָנַק (ʼânaq) / H602 is traced through Jeremiah 51:52, Ezekiel 9:4, Ezekiel 24:17, Ezekiel 26:15 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H602. anaq [ אָנַק ] verb cry, groan (Aramaic אֲנַק — Qal Imperfect יֶאֱנֹק Jer 51:52 ; Infinitive construct אֱנֹק Ezek 26:15 , both of groaning of wounded ( חָלָל ). Niph`al id. , in mourning, lamentation; Infinitive construct הֵאָנֵק Ezek 24:17 || אֵבֶל עָשָׂה ); Participle נֶאֱנָקִים 9:4 (|| נֶאֱנָחִים followed by עַל .

occurrences.englishText: “Therefore behold, the days come,” says Yahweh,

Yahweh said to him, “Go through the middle of the city, through the middle of Jerusalem, and set a mark on the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry over all the abominations that are done within it.”
Sigh, but not aloud. Make no mourning for the dead. Bind your headdress on you, and put your sandals on your feet. Don’t cover your lips, and don’t eat mourner’s bread.”
“The Lord Yahweh says to Tyre: ‘Won’t the islands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan, when the slaughter is made within you?
